predecessors.name: Ming dynasty
predecessors.text: the Ming lands Zhang Xianzhong took: Wuchang and Macheng (1643), 'much of Hunan', then Chongqing (25 July 1644), Chengdu (9 September 1644) and 'most of Sichuan province'

successors.name: Qing dynasty
successors.text: Sichuan: 'its territory fell to the forces of the Southern Ming and the Manchu-led Qing dynasty' (infobox); the page gives no boundary between them

successors.name: Southern Ming
successors.text: Sichuan: the same sentence names the Southern Ming; the generals' remnants 'held out in Sichuan, Yunnan, and Guizhou'

rulers.name: Zhang Xianzhong
rulers.title: Xi Wang (King of the West) 1643; emperor of the Xi, era name Dashun, from 1644

ledger.x: 1643: Zhang Xianzhong takes Wuchang and proclaims himself Xi Wang.
1644: Zhang takes Chengdu and the Xi rule most of Sichuan.

wars.name: Zhang Xianzhong's conquest of Sichuan
wars.outcome: Chongqing fell on 25 July 1644 and Chengdu on 9 September 1644; Ming loyalists retook Chongqing in spring 1645.

wars.name: Qing campaign against Zhang Xianzhong
wars.outcome: Zhang left Sichuan in October 1646 and was killed at Xichong on 2 January 1647 (infobox); the Xi ended.

certainty.note: A mobile rebel regime: the pages name cities (Wuchang, Chongqing, Chengdu) and provinces ('much of Hunan', 'most of Sichuan') but no boundary.
